† I. [כָּמַר] vb.Niph. grow warm and tender, be or grow hot (NH id. Pi. heat fruit in the ground, making it ripe, over-ripe, tender; Aramaic כְּמַר id., and more gen. make warm (one’s flesh, or food); cf. kemr, fermentation, etc., in mod. Syria WetzstZPV xiv (1891), 6)—
Niph. Pf. 3 pl. נִכְמְרוּ Gn 43:30 + 2 times, נִכְמָ֑רוּ La 5:10;— 1. grow warm and tender, fig., subj. רחמים; נ׳ רַחֲמָיו אֶל־אָחִיו Gn 43:30 (J), so נ׳ רַחֲמֶיהָ עַל־בְּנָהּ 1 K 3:26; (רַחֲמָ֑י We) יַחַד נ׳ נִחוּמָ֑י Ho 11:8 (‖ נֶהְפַּךְ עָלַי לִבִּי). 2. be or grow hot, עוֹרֵנוּ כְתַנּוּר נ׳ מִפְּנֵי וגו׳ La 5:10 our skin has become hot like a furnace, because of the famine.
